hero.title: The realm remembers.
hero.description: Enter a dark fantasy action RPG where dangerous magic, uneasy alliances and your choices shape the journey.
hero.intro: You survived what should have killed you. Beneath an old house, a mysterious Doll offers a way forward. Beyond its walls, villages cling to faith, a kingdom holds its breath, and something waits in the dark.

regions.name: The awakening
regions.description: A cage beneath an old house. A voice with answers of her own. Follow the Doll’s guidance into a village gathering, where even your first response can leave a lasting impression.

regions.name: Thornhallow
regions.description: A hidden community led by the Veyne sisters. Earn their trust, meet their withdrawn father and follow a family’s story from the quiet village to the heart of the Kingdom.

regions.name: Cairnhold
regions.description: Above the crowded streets, wealth and influence gather around the Crown. Below, ordinary people live with taxes, curfews and harsh justice—and the Thieves keep a society of their own.

regions.name: The Cult’s domain
regions.description: Ritual and sacrifice bind the Cult’s followers together. Seek answers among them, then face the ordeal waiting inside the Sixfold Crucible.

regions.name: Beyond the familiar
regions.description: The road reaches beyond the Kingdom: to the Templars of Iron Vow Hold, the Witch territories and the Plague Doctors who dwell there. Every place has its own loyalties.

characters.intro: A small companion with unsettling answers. She offers guidance, training and a way to travel—but trust is yours to give.
characters.detail: The Hidden Village’s ancestors created the Doll as a vessel for Dark magic. She gained a will of her own and now draws others toward bloodshed and ritual. The seal and the Doll are one and the same.
characters.name: The Cursed Doll

characters.intro: A priest who found renewed faith in a mysterious power. His conviction reaches far beyond the church doors.
characters.detail: The Doll guided Corven to a Relief and the village. He believed sacrifice fed his god and brought salvation. Seeking the Demon Father, he summoned the Nun instead. What he believes and what he has helped cause are very different things.
characters.name: Father Corven

characters.intro: A teacher of Holy magic who has sworn off casting. Reaching him means understanding the grief behind his retreat.
characters.detail: Garran accidentally harmed his wife with magic, and she died. He withdrew, leaving his daughters to lead the village. He can guide your own use of Holy magic, though he no longer casts it himself.
characters.name: Elder Garran Veyne

characters.intro: A master of Blood magic and protector of the King and Queen. His pursuit of power began with a wish to do good.
characters.detail: Garran’s son and the Veyne sisters’ brother, Lucan can become an ally against the Demon Father. If you march with the Cult, he stands as the Kingdom’s final defender. His Blood shield carries him and the royal couple to safety when the Kingdom falls.
characters.name: Lucan Veyne
The Veyne daughters
characters.intro: Tressa and Nerys lead Thornhallow. Get to know each sister: their trust and their support must be earned individually.
characters.detail: They are Garran’s daughters and Lucan’s sisters. After their mother’s death and their father’s withdrawal, they took responsibility for the village. Earning one sister’s support does not automatically earn the other’s.

characters.name: The Nun
characters.intro: A supernatural presence whose appearances lead you deeper into the mystery surrounding the village.
characters.detail: Corven’s summoning brought the Nun into the story. The attic and Crucible encounters take you through memories; her later sacrifice at the End Church brings forth the Demon Father.

characters.intro: At the Opera Hall, your past adventures become performances—and the audience has opinions.
characters.detail: Behind the Changelings lies the Opera Hall, where Pell stages stories from quests you have completed. Return to see familiar events in a different light.
characters.name: Pell

schools.description: Heal wounds, strengthen your defenses and hold enemies in place. Protect yourself—or support the people fighting beside you.
Turn your own health into power. Drain your enemies, move faster, summon a demon or protect yourself with a Blood Barrier.
Disappear, terrify your enemies and control the battlefield. Each cast brings you closer to lasting corruption.

faq.a: A dark fantasy action RPG about exploration, physical combat, powerful magic and personal choices. Travel through troubled communities, build relationships and decide where you stand.
Eclipsed Realms is in development. Release timing, supported platforms and where to buy the game have not been announced.
The campaign supports up to four players, with up to two local players on each machine. Join over a local network or with a direct address.

faq.q: Do we have to make the same choices?
faq.a: No. Your answers, relationships and personal consequences belong to your character. The host’s choices determine what physically happens in the shared world.

faq.q: Are Holy and Blood magic good and evil?
faq.a: A school of magic does not decide your morality. Holy magic can cause harm, and Blood magic can protect. Your actions tell your story.

faq.q: Will the guide spoil the story?
faq.a: The main site introduces the world without revealing its endings. Quest details, character secrets and ending explanations stay behind an optional spoiler switch on World & story.

faq.q: Where should I start with the guide?
faq.a: Begin with How to play for combat, magic and exploration essentials. Use the Player guide when you want details on a particular spell, weapon, ability or game system.

faq.q: Do I need to enter training to unlock fast travel?
faq.a: No. Discover a Doll travel destination during your journey to make it available. The station at the old house opens after its attic story encounter.

decisions.title: The hanging
decisions.setup: Two villagers are about to be hanged. Do you speak against the execution or support it?
decisions.consequence: Both villagers die. The game remembers whether you opposed or encouraged their deaths.
decisions.after: Nella’s later request about a runaway is a separate choice; it does not add another moral vote.

decisions.title: The courier
decisions.setup: Cultists have captured a courier. You can try to save him or encourage his captors.
decisions.consequence: The courier dies in either case. Your attempt to help still counts as a Good answer.
decisions.after: The captors and factions react to the answer you gave.

decisions.title: The village gate
decisions.setup: A wounded deserter asks for shelter. His pursuers demand that the village hand him over.
decisions.consequence: Protecting Iven gives him sanctuary. Surrendering him sends him away with Rusk in exchange for payment.
decisions.after: The daughters react when you return to the gate.

decisions.title: The royal hearing
decisions.setup: Evidence suggests Mara was coerced. The King asks for your judgment.
decisions.consequence: Defending Mara leads to house confinement and an investigation, not a pardon. Supporting the sentence condemns her and sends the evidence for destruction.
decisions.after: The Queen responds to what happened at the hearing.

decisions.title: The ritual
decisions.setup: Rusk is taking a captive’s breath into a vessel. You can break the connection or help him finish.
decisions.consequence: Breaking the connection lets Tamsin escape. Helping Rusk completes the draw; Tamsin goes still.
decisions.after: You can return to see what remains after the ritual.

entries.title: How damage is resolved
entries.summary: Attack damage, ratings, armor and hit material resolve first; the project then applies its combat rules.
body: The base calculation is AttackDamage × (1 + max(AttackRating, 0) / 100) ÷ (1 + max(Armor, 0) / 100) × hit-material multiplier. Armor is a divisor, so 100 Armor halves this stage of damage; it is not a flat damage subtraction. The attacking ability supplies the strike's damage and any ordinary critical multiplier.

Eclipsed Realms then applies a qualifying rear-hit multiplier, its additional stealth-critical check, immunity and damage modifiers, armor-family protection, final-boss rules, weapon passives and any damage redirect. Individual effects can supply their own armor scale or periodic damage path, so one universal calculator would hide important differences.

Physical and Magic are damage families. One-Handed, Two-Handed, Bow, Shield, Unarmed, Relief Melee and Relief Ranged are categories. Holy, Blood and Dark are schools. Held-Relief strikes are physical; Relief bolts and spells are classified at their source. Creature attacks carrying only a family are deliberately not reclassified as unarmed weapons.

entries.title: Critical hits
entries.summary: Stealth Rating controls the shared critical chance; technique criticals deal 1.5× damage before dagger bonuses.
body: The shared rule is 5 + 27.5 × (clamp(StealthRating, 0, 100) / 100)² percent. This produces 5% at rating 0, 11.875% at 50, and 32.5% at 100. Weapon techniques use this rule directly and add eligible stealth-perk chance before rolling.

A technique critical uses a 1.5× multiplier, increased by the additive critical-damage contribution of wielded daggers. A base dagger contributes 0.15, making a technique critical 1.65×; two base daggers total 1.80×.
warnings: Dagger contribution is confirmed for Eclipsed-owned technique criticals and the stealth-critical fallback. Do not claim the native Narrative basic-attack critical always receives it.

entries.title: Armor-family protections
entries.summary: Each qualifying armor piece adds 3 percentage points of its family's protection or healing benefit.
body: Knight and Templar pieces reduce Bow damage. Thief/Rogue and Guard pieces reduce One-Handed, Unarmed and held-Relief melee damage. Caster/Mage/Wizard pieces reduce Magic damage. Tattered and Villager pieces increase healing received from magic and food.

Pieces are added before applying the result: five qualifying pieces give 15%, rather than five multiplicative 3% reductions. Mixed sets contribute only the number of pieces matching each rule. These benefits are separate from the numerical Armor attribute.

A wielded shield separately reduces Two-Handed damage by 7%. Druid is recognized as an armor family but has no extra protection or healing row in this implementation. Creature attacks with no weapon category do not gain a false One-Handed or Unarmed classification.

entries.title: Blocking and guard armor
entries.summary: A valid frontal block adds temporary Armor for that hit; dual wielding uses the strongest guard once.
body: The frontal guard cone is 90° total, or 45° either side of the defender's facing. A qualifying blocked hit is resolved through ordinary damage with the weapon's guard bonus added to Armor for that one application. Side and rear hits receive no guard bonus.

Current guard bonuses are Shield +300; Greatsword, Greataxe, one-handed Sword, one-handed Axe and Dagger +150; Torch +15; Bow, Unarmed and Relief +10. With two wielded weapons, the highest eligible bonus is used once rather than summed.
Bow guard is enabled. The project owns guard armor and neutralizes Narrative's blanket blocking Armor so the per-hit table is not stacked with that older effect.
warnings: Older Atlas and source comments describe smaller values or flat absorption; the current implementation adds Armor to the normal divisor.

entries.title: Shield parries
entries.summary: Time an accepted shield-block press to the attacker's glow to negate a qualifying hit.
body: A wielded shield opens a 0.5-second parry window after an accepted block press, with at least 0.75 seconds between openings. Melee parries also require the press inside the attacker's visible timing window. The glow is aligned to predicted contact; it does not simply start at the beginning of every swing.

A successful parry refuses the hit, charges the blocked-hit stamina cost once, and staggers the melee attacker for a base 1 second, subject to crowd-control rules. The parry facing allowance is 90° either side of the defender and is a separate setting from the narrower ordinary guard-armor cone.

Ordinary arrows can be parried by a shield inside its window. The arrow deals no damage and charges block stamina, but does not stagger the archer or add Balance. Magic, weapon techniques, ultimates and offhand techniques are not parryable; the configuration explicitly leaves the techniques blockable.
warnings: Stamina cost is read from the actual Narrative blocked-hit effect; the C++ layer deliberately does not duplicate a fixed cost.

entries.title: Guard break
entries.summary: A defender who cannot pay the blocked-hit stamina cost takes the ordinary hit and loses the guard.
body: When a valid incoming block costs more stamina than the defender has left, the same attack is resolved once as ordinary damage with no guard-armor bonus. The remaining stamina is consumed down to zero and the block ability and parry window end.

The defender then receives a base 1-second Staggered status through the shared crowd-control rules. An immune target can avoid the stagger while still losing its stance. This stamina failure is separate from an attacker reaching the Balance disarm threshold.

entries.title: Balance and disarm
entries.summary: Parrying builds pressure on the attacker; a full Balance bar breaks their posture and can drop a weapon.
body: Each successful melee parry adds 40 Balance to the attacker. The bar caps at 100, so three parries without enough recovery cause a break. Ordinary landed hits add 0 Balance: health damage alone does not cause this form of weapon loss.

Recovery begins after 5 seconds without Balance damage and drains at 3 points per second. A Balance break uses a 1.5-second break stagger, replacing the ordinary parry stagger, and attempts a weapon drop.
Elite NPCs are protected from this Balance disarm unless they also count as bosses. Bosses and players are eligible; targets already marked Disarmed do not drop another weapon through this rule.
warnings: The bridge currently passes the plugin's offhand flag as false; avoid promising that an offhand parry always drops that specific offhand weapon.

entries.title: Parry counters and heavy knockdown
entries.summary: A successful parry opens a counter lunge and a short opportunity for a heavy knockdown.
body: After a melee parry, the defender's attack press can be held as a counter and the swing lunges toward the attacker. The counter target is tied to the attacker that was parried.

A heavy hit by the parrier can knock down that attacker within the greater of the resolved parry stagger and a 1.8-second window. This allows a heavy started during the stagger to land after its wind-up. The plugin's knockdown uses 1.6 seconds on the ground followed by get-up handling.

entries.title: Wielded weapon passives
entries.summary: Main-hand and offhand passive contributions add together; two-handed sword and axe contributions count twice.
body: Passives are enabled for player and NPC wielders. The system reads wielded weapons rather than every item carried in inventory. A weapon's family comes from the weapon-technique binding: Sword and Greatsword share Sword; Axe, Greataxe and Blunt use Axe; Dagger, Shield and Bow have their own families.

The ordinary damage pass applies sword penetration and on-hit axe or bow bleed to basic weapon hits. Technique hits, spells, burns and passive bleed are not treated as another ordinary weapon strike. Technique bleed does receive the axe bonus and shield reduction.

Mastered values are supported through weapon-mastery tags. Technique Mastery does not count automatically because bTechniqueMasteryCounts defaults to false. Base values should be presented as the normal reference, with mastered values clearly labeled.

entries.title: Sword: armor penetration
entries.summary: Wielded swords let ordinary weapon hits ignore a percentage of the target's Armor value.
body: One sword contributes 15% Armor penetration, or 20% when explicitly mastered. Greatswords contribute twice that amount: 30% base or 40% mastered. Multiple wielded contributions add before the total is clamped to 100%.

This reduces the target's Armor value, not a flat percentage of incoming damage and not the armor-family protection. Effective Armor is max(Armor, 0) × (1 − penetration / 100). The execution adjusts the already-computed hit by (100 + Armor) / (100 + effective Armor).

entries.title: Axe and blunt: bleeding
entries.summary: Axe-family hits cause a small bleed, and wielded axes increase the wielder's bleed damage.
body: One wielded axe contributes +15% bleed damage, or +20% with explicit mastery. A two-handed axe contributes +30% or +40%. Blunt-slot weapons intentionally retain the Axe-family passive.

An ordinary Axe-family hit creates a bleed equal to 5% of the hit's health damage over 4 seconds, then applies the wielder's captured axe bonus and the victim's current shield reduction. A base one-handed axe therefore yields 5.75 total bleed from a 100-damage hit before target reductions. Each application runs its own duration.

The victim's wielded shield is evaluated every tick, so equipping or dropping it during the bleed changes later ticks. Passive bleed does not apply Armor or armor-family protection again; immunity and other shared project modifiers still apply.

entries.title: Dagger: critical damage
entries.summary: Wielded daggers add points to critical damage in Eclipsed-owned critical calculations.
body: A dagger adds 15 percentage points of critical damage, or 20 with explicit mastery. This is an addition to the multiplier: 1.50× becomes 1.65× for one base dagger, or 1.80× with two base daggers.
The contribution is read directly by weapon-technique criticals. It also supplies the fallback multiplier for an extra stealth critical when the ability has no usable current multiplier.
warnings: This review did not verify universal dagger integration into ordinary Narrative basic-attack criticals.

entries.title: Shield: bleed resistance
entries.summary: A wielded shield reduces incoming weapon bleed and adds a separate defense against Two-Handed attacks.
body: The shield passive reduces bleed damage taken by 20%, or 30% with explicit weapon mastery. Passive bleed checks the currently wielded shield each tick. Weapon-technique bleed also passes through the shield reduction.

A shield's 7% reduction against Two-Handed attacks is an additional equipment-family rule. Its active frontal block uses +300 guard Armor. These are separate effects, so they should not be presented as one generic resistance percentage.

entries.title: Bow: one roll per arrow
entries.summary: An ordinary arrow chooses either armor penetration or bleed under the current default weights.
body: Each ordinary arrow hit rolls one server-side passive. Armor penetration and bleed each have weight 1, while critical damage has weight 0: the active default is an even split between two outcomes.

The penetration outcome ignores 7.5% of Armor, or 10% when explicitly mastered. The bleed outcome deals 7.5% of the arrow's health damage over 5 seconds, or 10% mastered. Bow bleed is never amplified by the Axe bonus, but the victim's shield still reduces it.

Critical-damage strengths exist in settings, but this project lacks a reliable per-arrow critical signal for that outcome. Its weight is disabled so an arrow cannot select a passive that does nothing.

entries.title: Torch: burning hits
entries.summary: Each wielded torch adds its own burn to a confirmed ordinary weapon hit.
body: The project configuration sets the burn reference to 40% of the torch's Attack Power. Ordinary burn uses half of that reference at base and the full reference after upgrade: 20% or 40% of torch Attack Power over 5 seconds.

The passive checks both main hand and offhand, and each unique wielded torch applies its own burn. It excludes blocked damage, technique damage, technique bleed and its own burn ticks from ordinary-hit triggering.
The older Atlas warning that Torch Sweep has no burn because the reference is unset is stale for this checkout: DefaultGame.ini now supplies the reference.

entries.title: Blindside and rear attacks
entries.summary: Blindside increases direct damage from behind; Shadow Step can add a one-hit rear bonus.
body: The rear cone is 70° total, centered behind the target. Blindside ranks grant +7.5%, +15% and +25% rear damage. It is a multiplier on the normal damage result and preserves the strike's already-calculated critical and Armor.
Only direct instant hits qualify. Periodic bleed and other duration effects do not qualify, and a target in the Blocking state does not grant the rear bonus or consume a pending Shadow Step bonus.
Shadow Step rank 2 adds 50 percentage points to the next qualifying rear hit against the enemy stepped to, within 5 seconds. With Blindside rank 3, that one hit receives +75% total rear damage.

entries.title: Unseen Edge and Silent Opening
entries.summary: Crouching against an unaware enemy adds critical-chance points, with a guaranteed first opening when learned.
body: Unseen Edge adds 50 percentage points of critical chance while crouched against an enemy whose awareness of that attacker is below Alert. Silent Opening adds 100 points on the first such attack against that enemy, making it guaranteed.

The bonuses are additive chance, not multipliers of the original chance: 10% plus Unseen Edge becomes 60%. The first-opening record is per attacker and enemy. When the enemy becomes aware, the mark clears so a later unaware encounter can have a new opening.

Technique attacks add the bonus to their own critical roll. Ordinary supported weapon attacks only perform an extra check if the ability did not already score a critical, preventing a second critical multiplier.

entries.title: Damage status modifiers
entries.summary: Shared status tags change damage dealt or taken in a defined order.
body: Mastered Fear makes a target take 20% more damage. Mastered Root makes its source deal 20% less damage. Mastered Dark Ascension makes its owner take 25% less damage and deal 35% more Dark-school damage. Pet Mastery adds 50% damage dealt.

Reaver's Fury adds 30% Physical-family damage and does not boost Magic-family damage. Relief immunity returns zero damage before these multiplier rows. Applicable source-dealt and target-taken rows multiply together, rather than adding their percentages into one bucket.

entries.title: Healing and receiving bonuses
entries.summary: Magic and food can benefit from worn armor, while Holy healing also responds to Karma.
body: Tattered and Villager pieces add 3% received healing each for magic and food. Five pieces grant +15%. Equipment regeneration and revival do not receive this family bonus.

Holy magic healing received gains +25% at Karma 25 or more, and +50% at Karma 50 or more. This is applied after the armor-family healing multiplier. Food and regeneration do not receive the Karma multiplier.
Pets accept Holy magic healing and regeneration; Blood or Dark healing and food do not reach them. Dead targets receive no healing through this path; revival is handled separately.

entries.title: Combat during eclipses
entries.summary: Eclipse strength adjusts Relief damage, selected creature damage and certain spell costs.
body: At full lunar or solar eclipse weight, Holy, Blood and Dark Relief damage gains 15%. Solar adds another 10% to Dark damage, totaling +25%, and gives Dark effects a further +10% effect multiplier.

Holy and Blood stamina costs are reduced by 10% per full eclipse weight; Dark stamina costs are unchanged by this rule. A full lunar eclipse reduces Blood health costs by 20%. Empowered creatures gain +15% damage under lunar weight or +25% under solar weight.
Bonuses scale with the live eclipse weight. An empowered creature casting a school spell takes the larger applicable damage bonus; the creature and school bonuses are not stacked on each other.

entries.title: Execution finishers
entries.summary: A recognized paired-scene finisher supplies lethal damage while preserving story protections.
body: During the actual execution scene, the damage calculation recognizes Narrative's execution-invulnerability effect on the attacker. For an eligible target it replaces ordinary weapon damage with max(calculated damage, current health, maximum health) + 1.

Target invulnerability still prevents damage through the attribute set. The final Mage and allied Demon Father are explicitly protected from the finisher shortcut; their hits continue through ordinary damage and finale-floor rules.
The execution check deliberately does not treat any generic Invulnerable or Busy tag as a finisher, so unrelated story invulnerability or ultimate abilities cannot turn an ordinary hit lethal.

entries.title: Flurry
entries.summary: Four rapid strikes with a short forward burst.
body: Four equal damage shares; lunge 1.7 → 2.2 m.

Base → Enhanced values are authored build-tool defaults. The player runtime cost is 50 Stamina; individual asset costs are overridden. Damage percentages are raw weapon Attack Power before mitigation.

entries.title: Sundering Thrust

entries.title: Weapon techniques and physical Ultimates
entries.summary: Ten technique families and nine physical Ultimate families form the current weapon-ability catalog.
body: Normal techniques: Flurry, Sundering Thrust, Rending Cleave, Executioner’s Arc, Falling Ruin, Arrowstorm, Skullcrusher, Torch Sweep, Savage Combination and King’s Reprisal. Physical Ultimates follow the main-hand weapon family; the shield has a technique but no registered physical Ultimate.

Every physical technique, from either hand and any family, shares one cooldown pool. Every physical Ultimate shares a separate pool. Using an ability sets that pool’s duration; the two pools do not block each other. Swapping equipment and respawning do not reset the PlayerState pools; pools are not written into saves.

Default physical Ultimates require their family unlock perk. Learned alternate Ultimates are selected per family. Technique mastery selects authored Enhanced values; physical Ultimates use a single value set.

Current player costs are 50 Stamina per technique and 100 per physical Ultimate, including unarmed and off-hand techniques. NPC techniques retain their authored costs. Current Config marks techniques, off-hand techniques and physical Ultimates as non-parryable; they remain blockable.

entries.title: Relief costs, cooldowns and progression
entries.summary: Holy spends Stamina, Blood sacrifices Health and Stamina, and Dark adds Dark Points.
body: Blood Health costs are percentages of Max Health. The caster must have strictly more Health than the sacrifice, so the cost cannot kill them. Costs and cooldowns commit at the spell’s visible release. Dark Points are accumulated at commitment; they are not a mana pool spent down.

Each school has four regular spells and a selectable slot-5 Ultimate. All Ultimates within one school share that school’s slot-5 cooldown, so switching does not bypass it. Holy, Blood and Dark have separate Ultimate tags.

Unlock, enhancement and mastery ranks apply by slot index. Slot N requires rank N; enhancement requires the slot to be unlocked, and mastery requires enhancement. NPC spell access and tiers come from their NPC magic configuration.

Native costs and durations can be modified at runtime. Eclipse code reduces Holy/Blood Stamina costs, and lunar effects reduce Blood Health sacrifices. Corrupted-player Dark cooldown reduction and mastered Dark Ascension can shorten Dark cooldowns.

Two numeric corrections matter: Summon Demon now costs 25% Max Health, and Savage Combination costs 50 Stamina for players despite its older authored 25 value. Torch burn is enabled by the current 40% AP reference Config.

entries.title: Crowd control and movement statuses
entries.summary: Root, fear, knockdown, freeze, stagger and slow have distinct effects on movement and actions.
body: Rooted prevents movement while still allowing attacks and turning. Frozen stops movement and actions; the freeze application cancels running abilities and holds the target's pose.

Feared NPCs flee from the source, cannot attack while their combat activities are suspended, then resume normal behavior. Knocked Down covers the push, downed period and recovery. Staggered is the recoil caused by a parried attack and prevents attacks. Slowed reduces movement without freezing the target.
A Fear cast from a different allied player adds its resolved duration to a running Fear. Overlapping casts that do not qualify for allied stacking keep the longest end time.

entries.title: Resistance, immunity and parry stagger
entries.summary: NPC tier does not automatically grant crowd-control immunity.
body: Crowd-control rules may match an NPC tier and an optional target tag. Matching duration multipliers multiply together; any matching immunity refuses the status.
The current project configuration contains no tier-resistance rules, and the native default rule list is empty. Do not assume bosses or elites resist control simply because of their tier.
Parry stagger skips tier-based resistance. Only explicit protections tied to a required target tag on a tier-agnostic rule remain eligible.

entries.title: Damage, drain and mastery statuses
entries.summary: Curse, Bleeding and Blood Siphon apply ongoing pressure; mastered control also changes damage.
body: Cursed marks Curse damage over time. Bleeding is the mastered Blood Rupture damage-over-time status. Blood Siphon marks a target drained by a Relief tether.
Mastered Fear makes the affected target take 20% more damage. Mastered Binding Light makes the rooted target deal 20% less damage. These multipliers belong to the combat modifier layer.

Mastered Blood Rush improves stamina regeneration, while mastered Blood Offering grants lifesteal on damage dealt. Their exact spell durations and recovery values are defined by their individual spell entries.

entries.title: Protection and beneficial statuses
entries.summary: Relief buffs cover armor, recovery, movement, concealment, empowerment and transformation.
body: Holy Armor adds armor. Blood Offering restores resources over time and grants attack/armor bonuses. Blood Rush increases movement speed. Divine Renewal is a healing aura. Dark Invisibility conceals the caster and restores over time.

Dark Continuance grants an attack buff and preserves Dark casting permission. Empowered identifies an enhanced summon with increased health and damage. Old Man Armor stacks with Holy Armor; Old Man Renewal supplies healing over time.

Blood Barrier rejects harmful effects while Relief casting costs still apply. The separate Immune status makes incoming damage zero and is used by mastered Invisibility. Mastered Dark Ascension multiplies Dark damage by 1.35 and incoming damage by 0.75.

entries.title: Animal taming and eligible species
entries.summary: Each player can keep one pet; eligible species depend on Animal Taming rank and corruption.
body: Rank 1 permits goat, deer, moose and cow. Rank 2 adds bear and mutant bear. Demon Goat and Minotaur require rank 4 and corruption in the current shipped configuration.
The interaction has a 2-second hold followed by 3 seconds of taming, within a 450 cm range. An existing pet is released only when the new bond completes.
A pet follows the owner's level. Pets do not receive their own XP, crime or karma progression.

entries.title: Pet mastery, healing and targeting
entries.summary: Taming Mastery improves a pet's health, regeneration and damage in three stages.
body: Mastery rank 1 adds 20% maximum health. Rank 2 raises regeneration from 5% to 10% of maximum health each second. Rank 3 grants 50% more damage.
Pets accept Holy magic healing and regeneration. Food, Blood healing and Dark healing do not heal pets. Dead pets require revival.

Automatic targeting normally selects threats; when the owner or pet is below 35% health, the pet favors its owner's target. Target hold is 2 seconds, threat memory is 8 seconds and threat range is 3500 cm. Catch-up moves a pet beside its owner after it remains more than 3000 cm away for 6 seconds.

entries.title: Pet death, revival and dismissal
entries.summary: A fallen pet has a five-minute revival window.
body: Revival uses a 5-second hold at the pet's revival site. The pet returns at 15% health with a 3-second get-up. The saved revival window can outlive the visible body; expiry removes the pet.
When the owner dies, the pet dies with them. Dismissal sends the animal toward its home and releases the bond; after 120 seconds it gives up the journey and remains wild where it stands.

entries.title: Companion allegiance and assistance
entries.summary: A companion belongs to one exact owner and assists against NPC threats.
body: Companions follow their owner and can assist against NPCs that damage the owner or receive damage from the owner. Attack commands refuse the owner, the owner's other companions, non-NPC targets and dead targets.

The owner and companion cannot harm each other. This protection is tied to their bond; it does not make the companion universally friendly. Party rules separately protect allies and their affiliated companions.

Stop Following keeps the companion's allegiance and party presence while it waits. Dismissal removes follow and assist goals and returns the NPC to ordinary behavior. Relief summons use the companion system.

entries.title: Normal, Elite and Boss behavior
entries.summary: Combat tier changes decision behavior; campaign run tier separately scales NPC health and damage.
body: An NPC without a Boss or Elite tag is Normal. Bosses and elites re-plan pursuit against an escaping target; normal NPCs retain deliberate pursuit pacing. An unreachable target is abandoned after the default 3 seconds and can be reacquired when a route returns or it damages the NPC.

Ordinary elites enter phase two at 50% health, increasing walk, sprint and slow-walk speeds by 50%. This transition itself does not increase damage or health. Registered two-phase final bosses use their own encounter phase system.

Campaign difficulty multiplies maximum health and outgoing damage by 1.0 in New Game, 1.2 in NG+ and 1.4 in NG++. Current implementation applies this to all NPCs, including neutrals, friendlies and companions. Bosses ignore the ally-spacing restriction.

entries.title: NPC blocking and stamina
entries.summary: NPCs react to observed attacks and spend stamina using the player stamina model.
body: NPC stamina reads its base maximum and regeneration from the player's default attribute asset, starts full on spawn/revive and uses the shared regeneration pause after expenditure. Equipment and effects can modify these values.

Blocking depends on loadout, combat tier and the NPC's Block Tendency. Shield users are more likely to guard than ordinary melee users. Current code also supports a weak bow guard when bow blocking is enabled.

Base shield block chance is 55% against melee and 45% against ranged attacks; other guard loadouts start at 25% and 10%. Elite and Boss multipliers are 1.4 and 1.3, before Block Tendency and the final 85% cap. Shield users may time a guard for a parry.
warnings: Base stamina attributes are loaded from a Blueprint gameplay-effect asset; this article does not treat the header's historical measured asset values as a fresh asset inspection.

entries.title: Group combat and caster coordination
entries.summary: NPCs sharing a target coordinate spell timing, melee turns and positions.
body: NPC cast starts against a shared target are separated by 1.2 seconds. Allies avoid starting the same spell class on that target within 6 seconds. One crowd-control slot is reserved through casting and for 8 seconds after release, and remains occupied while the target actually carries control.

Damage-spell scores double while a control opening is reserved or active. The normal cap is two melee attackers per target, reduced to one against a knocked-down target; at most one melee turn belongs to a Relief caster. Turns rotate after 10 seconds when someone is waiting, without interrupting a swing.
Waiting melee NPCs hold around 650 cm away, casters use a 700–1400 cm band and formation slots aim for at least 250 cm between allies. Bosses are excluded from this formation control.

entries.title: NPC food and hydration recovery
entries.summary: NPC food and hydration statuses provide recovery without a hunger simulation.
body: NPC statuses are static: they do not decay and there is no eating or drinking AI. A food status supplies its mapped consumable's base health recovery; hydration supplies base stamina recovery, without player perk scaling.
Well Fed maps to Full Meal, Fed to Hearty Dish and Hungry to Light Fare. Starved supplies no food recovery. Hydrated, Thirsty and Parched use Energy Drink recovery; Dehydrated supplies none.

Recovery activates only while the relevant attribute is below maximum and ends at maximum or on death. There is one effect of each kind per NPC; reevaluation replaces it instead of stacking. Authored or saved status changes update recovery.

entries.title: Food, water and consumable capacity
entries.summary: Food and water are separate fullness pools that limit when recovery consumables can be used.
body: Base food capacity is 100 and base water capacity is 50. Each of four capacity ranks adds 25 to its pool, reaching 200 food or 150 water. Consumption is refused if the item's full consumption amount would exceed remaining capacity.
Food tiers are Well Fed, Fed, Hungry and Starved; water tiers are Hydrated, Thirsty, Parched and Dehydrated. Thresholds are 75%, 50%, 25% and 0% of the current maximum.

Base depletion is 5 from each pool per calibrated 60-second interval. Preservation reduces depletion by 10% per rank, up to three ranks. Current depletion tracks elapsed Narrative game time, including Wait skips; offline time does not drain. Arena play suspends depletion and does not bank it for later.

entries.title: Utility perks and recovery timing
entries.summary: Utility improves stamina efficiency, consumable recovery and the delay before regeneration resumes.
body: Conditioning increases stamina regeneration by 25%. Evasive reduces dodge stamina cost by 25%; Guarded reduces block costs, including blocked-hit stamina, by 25%.

Stamina regeneration pauses for 1 second after spending stamina. Recovery halves the delay to 0.5 seconds. Its choices add 25 carry capacity through Pack Rat or 10 Stealth Rating through Light Footed.

Food Recovery and Water Recovery add 25% recovery per rank, up to four ranks. Sustenance adds 15%; Nourished adds 25% to food health recovery and Refreshed adds 25% to drink stamina recovery. These recovery bonuses add together in the corresponding multiplier; they do not extend the item's normal duration.

entries.title: Corruption and Dark magic
entries.summary: Reaching 100 Dark Points permanently corrupts the character and changes combat tradeoffs.
body: Corruption latches at 100 Dark Points; lowering points afterward does not cure it. Maximum health, maximum stamina and stamina regeneration are each reduced by 10%, applied once rather than stacked. Corruption adds no faction membership.

Dark spell cooldowns become 25% shorter. Invisibility lasts 25% longer, Void Pulse pushes 25% farther and Fear lasts 25% longer. These corruption bonuses apply to Dark magic; Blood and Holy spells receive no equivalent bonus.
Corrupted characters cannot cast Holy magic, although they may still own and equip the Holy Relief. Corruption also participates in the rank-4 Demon Goat and Minotaur taming requirements.

entries.title: Party protection and friendly fire
entries.summary: Party members cannot harm or control each other; combat between strangers requires mutual opt-in.
body: Same-party protection covers weapons, techniques, Relief spells, damage over time, traps, projectiles, companions and summons. Beneficial healing and buffs remain allowed.

Current rules also protect players outside the same party unless both enable friendly fire. A vengeance mark does not bypass this requirement. Leaving a party removes its specific protection but still leaves the stranger opt-in rule.
Arena worlds use their own team rules. The final battle can temporarily place party members on opposing encounter sides, allowing combat between those sides without changing their party membership.

entries.title: Co-op downing and revival
entries.summary: An eligible fallen player gets a 60-second chance for a living teammate to revive them.
body: Downing requires another living human party member; the split-sides finale additionally requires the same side. A teammate revives at the body through the shared 5-second hold interaction, restoring 15% health in place.

After revival, that player cannot be downed again for one real-time hour. The cooldown persists by save identity, so waiting in game, reloading and travel cannot shorten it. Solo play, no available reviver, active cooldown, arena play and the attic defeat retain their immediate death handling.

An unrevived campaign guest receives Settings and Main Menu without session respawn. An unrevived host fails the campaign session for guests; guests follow when the host continues. PvP deaths and the split-sides finale have their own handling.

entries.title: PvP death and vengeance
entries.summary: Recent non-party player damage routes a death through Yield or Seek Vengeance.
body: A death counts as PvP when a non-party player damaged the victim within the previous 30 seconds, even if an NPC delivers the final blow. Eligible party revival is still available.
If unrevived, the victim can Yield to respawn without penalty or Seek Vengeance to respawn and mark every player involved in that damage window. A PvP death never fails the campaign.
Vengeance marks are saved for the victim and track a marked player while online and alive. A mark clears when that marked player dies by any cause. Marks do not override mutual friendly-fire opt-in.

entries.title: Arena rounds, builds and loadouts
entries.summary: Arena combat uses temporary builds, team elimination and a fresh random loadout every round.
body: The arena expansion is enabled. Native build defaults set fighters to level 100 with all skills maxed. Current runtime forces a new random loadout every round; the older once-per-match option is ignored.

Only opposing teams can damage each other during the active round. Staging, preparation and countdown are protected. There is no round respawn; elimination or remaining out of bounds beyond the grace period removes a fighter. Timeout or simultaneous elimination gives a draw without a point.

Defaults are a 3-second countdown, 180-second round limit, 3-second out-of-bounds grace and 5-second round-end interval. Multiplayer is first to three wins; the solo build default is first to two. Arena actions do not award campaign kill XP or trigger karma, crime, reputation or NPC-memory consequences. Food and water do not drain.

entries.title: Core Traits
entries.summary: Five traits shape your character for the journey: Strength, Agility, Stamina, Vitality, and Charisma.
body: Each displayed allocation point represents five underlying points. Every trait caps at five displayed points (25 underlying). The full journey budget must be spent: 12 displayed points in New Game, 18 in NG+, and 25 in NG++.

Strength adds Attack Rating; Agility adds Stealth Rating; Stamina and Vitality increase their maximum resource pools; Charisma seeds starting social standing. Core attributes are committed for the journey rather than earned on level-up.

entries.title: New Game+ and New Game++
entries.summary: The campaign tier multiplies NPC health and outgoing attack damage.
body: Current runtime code applies the campaign multiplier to every NPC, including neutral actors, friendlies, and companions. Becoming a companion changes allegiance and behavior, not this multiplier.

Maximum health is multiplied directly. Attack Rating is multiplied and receives an additional 100 × (multiplier − 1), so the damage rating factor scales by the same multiplier. Refreshing the effect keeps the current health fraction.

entries.title: Levels and experience
entries.summary: Levels use the project’s inherited experience curve; Core Traits do not rise automatically with each level.
body: Narrative’s native level function truncates 0.07 × √XP and adds one. Its inverse threshold function is ((level − 1) / 0.07)². Blueprint or configured overrides can alter the defaults; they were not freshly inspected here.
The native character defaults do not reapply base attributes on each level-up. The old balancer’s universal linear health curve is therefore not evidence of actual player or enemy HP at each level.

entries.title: Horse riding (Eclipsed horse)
entries.summary: Players ride Narrative's horse with project-added reverse, turn-in-place, carved turns, sprint and a hold-to-brake dismount; weapons are put away for the whole ride.
body: Look at a horse and press Interact to get on. Forward riding and steering are the Narrative add-on's own; pulling back walks the horse slowly backwards, sideways at a standstill pivots it on the spot and sideways while moving carves a wider turn. Left Shift (pad L3) sprints. Pressing Interact while moving fast brakes the horse and then gets you off. Any drawn weapon is holstered when you mount and cannot be drawn while seated.

entries.title: Fog of war and map exploration
entries.summary: Each player's own explored area is remembered per map and saved with that player; unexplored ground is black on the minimap and world map.

User direction 2026-10-03: unexplored ground black, not a darkening (recorded in EclipsedMapMarkers.h:175 and session-ledger-2026-10-02h).

entries.title: Locks, keys and lock picking
entries.summary: Locked chests and doors open with the right key from your real inventory, or by a timing lock-pick challenge whose misses make noise and whose attempts are recorded as lock tampering.
body: A locked chest or door offers Unlock if you carry its key, otherwise Pick Lock. Picking is a short timing challenge (3-5 prompts depending on difficulty) answered with Interact; a miss makes a real noise nearby NPCs can hear, and being seen tampering is a crime where the local law judges it so. Walking away abandons the attempt.
warnings: Proven on a blank fixture map only; not in the open world and not in multiplayer (migration-2026-10-04 note 2).

entries.title: Pickpocketing
entries.summary: Crouched behind an NPC, or beside a sleeping one, the player picks items from its real inventory; failure alerts the victim and makes noise.
body: Sneak up crouched behind an NPC (or next to a sleeping one), within reach, and choose Pickpocket to see what it carries. Each item is a separate server roll and higher Stealth improves the odds. Failing keeps the item with the NPC, alerts it, makes a noise and records a pickpocket incident; equipped items cannot be taken.
warnings: A remote client's pickpocket was not run in the multi-process tests (ledger row R11 remaining).

entries.title: Ownable item pickups (theft)
entries.summary: World item pickups can have an owner; taking an owned item always works but is theft, prompted as 'Steal' and witnessed only by NPCs who actually see it.

entries.title: Day/night clock, day phases, curfew and alerts
entries.summary: One coordinator reads Narrative's 0-2400 clock and world facts to publish day phase, curfew and settlement alert changes that encounters, NPC life and stations react to.
body: The sky follows Narrative's time of day (Ultra Dynamic Sky add-on). The world changes with it: night-only encounters appear at night, curfew runs from 22:00 to 05:00 unless a story fact overrides it, and a settlement's alert level drops one step for every 4 game hours without a new crime report. The HUD shows Morning / Afternoon / Evening / Night.
warnings: Two phase schemes coexist: rule phases (Dawn/Day/Dusk/Night) drive gameplay, HUD bands (Morning/Afternoon/Evening/Night) are display only.
The HUD band hours were chosen in code; the user decision E-062 names the labels only.

entries.title: Weather (Ultra Dynamic Weather via Narrative)
entries.summary: Weather is Narrative's Ultra Dynamic Sky add-on (saved with the game); the project reads its current state for the HUD and story encounters change it with Narrative's weather event.

entries.title: Torch (carried light weapon)
entries.summary: The torch is Narrative's demo torch weapon with a project Torch Sweep technique and a burn passive whose strength is still unset, so it currently deals no burn.

E-026: torch weapon + technique; burn = 50% / 100% of the verified axe bleed total; second application after 2 s. E-045: the description states what the torch currently does.

entries.title: NPC relationships (per player)
entries.summary: Each player has their own relationship score with each socially identified NPC, changed by dialogue events and read by dialogue conditions.
body: Helping or harming named NPCs changes how they regard you; another co-op player keeps a separate relationship. Dialogue options can require a relationship level.
warnings: The main game built much more social behaviour on top (awareness, ties, responses); the sandbox has only the base relationship model.

entries.title: Faction reputation
entries.summary: Each player has their own -100..+100 standing with each Narrative faction, changed by identified witnesses' rules, authored dialogue/quest events and story encounters - never by Narrative's alliance map.
body: Factions remember what you did in front of their people. Start Village, Hidden Village, Cultists, Kingdom and Thieves start at 0 plus your creation Charisma. Bands: -100 extreme negative, -99..-50 Disliked, -49..49 Neutral, 50..99 Friendly, 100 extreme positive. Cards show lines such as 'Start Village reputation -3'.
warnings: No consumer was found that turns low reputation into hostility or service refusal (limited search of Source).
Witness rules now cover all five factions (Kingdom and Thieves added 2026-10-12; Cultists have a killing rule but no assault rule). Balance values are placeholders.

Eclipsed Peds (Kingdom) witness and change Kingdom reputation but have no SocialIdentity, so no per-player relationship; demons, creatures, dolls, jester, templar and witch NPCs have no faction (design open).

entries.title: Karma
entries.summary: A per-player moral score from -100 to +100, changed by identified witnesses' rules, by every contributor's share of an NPC's death Karma, and by authored dialogue and story events.
body: Karma tracks broad conduct, separate from reputation, relationships, personality and Dark Points. A 'Karma +/-N' notification appears on every real change and the Social & Codex page shows it. Dark magic is not automatically a Karma matter.
warnings: Two writers on a kill: witness-gated rule Karma (killer only) and unconditional death Karma (every contributor) (disc.no-witness-still-karma).
No Karma bands are authored, so threshold-based content has nothing to read.
Consumers found: dialogue conditions, world conditions (bCheckKarma), reaction scoring, the Social & Codex page; the pawn's Karma costume path is Blueprint (not inspected).
[sandbox] No Karma thresholds were authored in either project at migration time (migration-log A.11 K.5).

entries.title: Witness evaluation (did it see you?)
entries.summary: For each incident every nearby NPC with a matching rule is checked once: did it see the act itself, and could it tell which player did it?
body: An NPC only holds something against you if it actually saw the act and recognised you. Behind its back, out of range, through a wall, or while you are invisible or fully stealthed, it sees nothing - or sees 'something' but not who (no personal consequence). A victim always knows it was hit, but must have seen you to blame you.
warnings: Identification is instant (no gradual suspicion) for violence and magic; the gradual model exists only in the stealth layer.
NPCs without a matching rule never witness - they at most 'hear' an assault or death (HeardDisturbance, no culprit) even if they watched.
The -EclipsedLegacyWitnessSight switch restores the old line of sight for A/B diagnostics only.

entries.title: Direct-witness memory
entries.summary: When an identified witness's rule says so, 'this NPC saw this player do this' is saved in that player's own record, per individual NPC, for dialogue, quests and the card's 'Witnessed by' list.
body: NPCs remember what they personally saw you do, and only you: the same guard can know Player 1 assaulted someone and know nothing about Player 2. The consequence card's 'Witnessed by:' names exactly those who will remember. When a witness dies, its personal memories of you are removed.
warnings: Dialogue condition and Forget event match the NPC definition's CharacterID, not the individual: every City Guard answers for what one City Guard saw (disc.witness-condition-by-definition).
Offline players' memories of a witness who dies are cleaned only when they reconnect (consequence-depth-pass#7).
Bribes and serving a sentence never clear memories (ledger-guards-arrest-jail#R19, #R23).

entries.title: NPC knowledge ledger (awareness)
entries.summary: Separate from the player-side consequences, the world keeps what each individual NPC knows about each incident - how it learned it, whom it blames and how sure it is - and that knowledge spreads only through real sources.
body: NPCs know things only by seeing, hearing a disturbance, finding a body, being the victim, being told, or authored story knowledge. Hearsay weakens with every retelling; a guard who receives a report shares it with up to three nearby colleagues once. A dead NPC's knowledge dies with it, and a respawned person starts fresh.
warnings: Only rule-matched witnesses become observers; everyone else at most hears.
Two knowledge stores exist: per-player direct-witness memory (player save) and this per-NPC ledger (world save).
The incidental reaction system (perception area) reads this ledger for its 'known crime' tier.

entries.title: Stolen goods record
entries.summary: Each stolen inventory stack remembers whom it was taken from, how and in which incident - saved with the player - but nothing in the game acts on it yet.

warnings: Arrest confiscation treats stolen items like any other item.
Should stolen goods matter anywhere (merchants, guards, confiscation)? No design found.

entries.title: Arrest, jail and reclaiming belongings
entries.summary: Accepting arrest fades the offender's own view, takes their belongings into custody and locks them in a Kingdom dungeon cell; serving the sentence is free and instant, and belongings wait in a chest outside.
body: After 'I'll come quietly' your screen fades, your carried and equipped items (except quest items tagged Keep On Arrest) are taken, and you wake locked in a cell. Interact with the cell door twice within 5 seconds to serve your sentence - no waiting, no time skip, no fine. Then reclaim your things at the belongings chest; whatever does not fit stays there safely. Disconnecting, dying or reloading puts you back in your cell.
warnings: First relocation into the dungeon can hold ~40 s on a dark screen while the interior streams.
Partial (full bag) restore, crash mid-transfer, reconnect and World Partition unload not run (R24, R25, R40); Relief-deployed arrest not run (R22).

entries.title: Bribing the guard
entries.summary: With the secret Speech perk Attuned Speaker and enough gold, a confronted player can pay the lead guard: 100 gold for the first distinct offense, +100 per further offense, at most 2000.
body: The bribe reply only appears with the Attuned Speaker perk, enough money and a bribable case (never for assaulting royalty). Paying makes the whole group stand down, but only the paid guard will ignore later reports of that same incident; witnesses still remember, and a new crime needs a new payment.
warnings: Full civilian flee-and-report route to a paid guard not run (R19).

entries.title: Contextual conversations (later reactions)
entries.summary: What an NPC knows decides which contextual conversation it has for you next: a friendly warning, a confrontation, reconciliation, a second-hand accusation, refused service, family harm or help, gratitude or a body report.
body: Talk to an NPC who saw your crime within a game day and it confronts you; later it offers reconciliation. A merchant with an unresolved concern refuses service. Someone told about you accuses you second-hand. A guard who likes you (relationship 25+) and was told the watch is after you walks over and warns you quietly. Those you rescued thank you. Protected story NPCs (the Nun) always keep their own dialogue, and nobody invites you while fighting.

entries.title: Character creator (Appearance / Attributes / Personality)

body: New Game (and Host Game) opens the creator. Title arrows, LT / RT or Page Up / Down turn between APPEARANCE, ATTRIBUTES and PERSONALITY. While anything is missing, Confirm & Exit is dimmed and cannot be pressed (the hold-to-create key is ignored) and the footer lists what is still needed. With a pad, A on the name row opens an on-screen keyboard. On Create a confirmation appears; then the character enters the world and the choices are applied once. The Character Creator is no longer offered from the pause menu.
Creator owns all character choices (E-041); host creation before the listen server (E-023); Darklands / custom art presentation (E-025, hud-art R55).

You place 15 points in steps of 5 over Witty (clever, disarming replies), Empathetic (kindness and understanding) and Bold (direct, commanding replies). All 15 must be placed before you can create the character. These become your real personality scores, which keep growing with the replies you choose.

entries.title: Personality traits (Bold / Witty / Empathetic)
entries.summary: Three personality tracks seeded in the creator and grown by the reply styles you choose in dialogue; every real change shows a HUD notice.

A real change shows a notice such as 'Personality: Bold +2' (not for the creator's seed or for loading a save). Content can check a minimum score or your dominant style, and some NPCs like or dislike a style, which changes your relationship with them.
Final styles Bold / Witty / Empathetic; Karma separate (compatibility-audit section 4). Legacy Cruel/Cunning/Compassion nodes are logged no-ops.

entries.summary: A campaign session admits at most four human players across all machines; a joining machine's whole local group is checked before anyone loads.

entries.title: Couch co-op (split-screen, 2 per machine)
entries.summary: A second player joins on the same computer with their own gamepad and plays in a left/right split screen, also inside an online session.
body: Player 2 presses Start on a second controller during gameplay to join; the screen splits left/right. Player 2 leaves from their own pause menu by holding View/Back; their character is saved first and player 1 is unaffected. Keyboard, mouse and the first gamepad belong to player 1.
Session g brief (couch join with Start / hold-to-leave); integration audit 2026-10-07: 2+2 couch-online.
warnings: Only simulated/virtual second gamepads were exercised; unplugging pad 2 mid-game is not handled (handoff-2026-10-02g).

Couch seat 2 has no character creator; since 2026-10-07 no seat opens the in-game attribute screen, so seat 2 gets the default allocation (E-041, ledger-playtest-2026-10-07b#R48; E-027's couch clause predates this).
usage-manual-2026-10-02g still says only the host machine can add a couch player; current code lets a client split-join its guest.

PRODUCT REGRESSION (found 2026-10-24 by the 8121 couch proof, 72/18): the 'hold View to leave' prompt never armed in real play because IsPauseMenuOpenFor only recognised the stock W_NarrativeMenu_Pause_C while the game (E-093) opens W_NarrativeMenu_Pause_Eclipsed_C. Fix (stock class OR class name starting with W_NarrativeMenu_Pause) compiled 8122, proof pending (post8122 chain). Validation lowered to compiled until that leg passes; see disc.couch-leave-prompt-pause-widget-class.

entries.title: Co-op saving (one file per player + world once)
entries.summary: Every save request in a session is executed by the host: one file per connected player and the shared world once, coalesced when several systems ask in the same frame.
body: Saving from the pause menu, a checkpoint or a quest saves everybody's character and the world together. A leaving host and a leaving couch guest are saved first. While a Jester performance runs, nobody can save.

entries.title: Personal story flags vs shared world flags
entries.summary: Each player's story choices and once-only rewards are saved in their own record, while world facts are shared by everyone in the campaign and saved in the world file.
body: Your conversations, choices and one-time rewards are yours: a friend completing a scene does not complete it for you, and being in the party alone never earns a once-only reward. Facts about the world (a door opened, a scene played, a boss dead, an ending chosen) are the same for everybody.
Story first pass 2026-10-03: story flags player-specific by design; world flags shared.
warnings: Hidden Village and Changeling co-op legs were not run with two players (ledger-batch-2026-10-05#R50; ledger-changeling#R20).

entries.title: Per-player quests and quest markers
entries.summary: Each player has their own quests, quest-giver markers and objectives; Narrative's party quests and party dialogue run through the shared party component.
body: Quest-giver '!' and '?' markers reflect your own progress (a friend may see '?' where you see '!'). Objective markers show only for the player who owns the task, and a '!' shows only within 300 m of you. In a party, Narrative forwards completed quest tasks to the party's shared quests.
E-054 one symbol per NPC per player, '?' outranks '!'; E-057 '!' only under 300 m from that local player.
warnings: The 300 m range per local player was not run in multiplayer (ledger-batch-2026-10-10#R40).
Quest tracker per player ran in one process only (ledger-playtest-2026-10-07b#R30).

entries.title: LAN session discovery (incl. Shipping)
entries.summary: Hosted games are found on the local network through the Null online subsystem, filtered by build, and diagnosed in a support log that never confuses direct joins with discovery.
body: Games hosted on the same network appear in Browse Games with free seats and ping. If nothing answers, the multiplayer diagnostics log explains the usual firewall and network causes.
warnings: Two physical machines on a LAN and internet sessions are not tested; discovery without a firewall allowance for the exe was not re-tested.
The product exe has no firewall rule until Windows asks on its first host (allow Private for LAN play).

entries.title: Join Game / Browse Games
entries.summary: Players browse co-op games hosted on their network and join either with a newly created character or with the character they already have on that host.
body: Join Game opens BROWSE GAMES. Refresh searches the network; each listed game offers 'Create character + join' (the character creator opens first, then you join wearing that character) or 'Join with my character' (your existing record on that host). JOIN BY ADDRESS offers the same two choices for a typed host address. Games for another build, private games, full games and other session types are hidden.
warnings: Two physical machines and internet joins were never tested; every recorded join ran on one computer.
The Shipping proof drove Browse Games with real mouse clicks; a gamepad pass through the dashboard is not named.

entries.title: Leaving a session and host departure
entries.summary: Leaving returns a player to the main menu with a reason; when the host leaves, the campaign is saved first and every guest is sent back with 'The host ended the session'.
body: A guest who leaves goes back to the main menu and their seat frees up. If the host quits, the campaign is saved and everyone else returns to the menu with 'The host ended the session. Your character data is intact.' Lost connections, refused joins and failed travel also bring you back to the menu with the reason shown.
warnings: Host migration is not supported (the session ends when the host leaves).
A disconnect mid-cinematic (camera restrictions, equipment grants) was not exercised (ledger-integration-audit-2026-10-07#R22).

entries.title: Jester performances in co-op
entries.summary: With more than one player, a Jester performance replays a finished tale for the performer alone; the world is not rolled back, the performer's gains are reverted afterwards, and nobody can save while it runs.
body: A player who finished a tale can watch it again at the Jester stage. In co-op only that player is staged: they leave the party for the show, the cast is hostile only to them, and when it ends their XP, items and quests return to what they were. Other players keep playing and keep their own gains, but no one can save until the show ends. Tales that change the shared world can only be performed alone.
Decision D7 (co-op Jester isolation): refused through 2026-10-01; session g item 4 lifted the guard with performer-scoped co-op performances.
warnings: Co-op is unverified on the latest replay code: EclipsedJesterReplay changed again on build 8295 after the 8257 proof (ledger-playtest-2026-10-07b#R68).
The JesterReplay.h comment says other players keep playing normally, but nobody can save during a performance.

entries.title: Travel and the Cursed Doll network in co-op
entries.summary: Every player travels on their own; the Training Arena is one shared session that players enter and leave individually, each returning to their own origin.
body: Fast travel and entrances move only you; your friends stay where they are. In the Training Arena a friend can join your running session from any Doll and keeps their own way home; the session closes when the last player leaves. Discovering a Doll waypoint gives each player 100 XP once.
E-020 Doll destination rule; batch 2026-10-05 Doll network brief (one shared arena, per-player origins).
warnings: 3-4 player arrivals and per-player discovery XP in co-op were not run (ledger-batch-2026-10-05#R2, #R15).
Door interiors in multiplayer: conflicting reports (see disc.coop-door-player0).

entries.title: Jester performances (quest replay)
entries.summary: The Jester restages quests this character already lived; afterwards the campaign returns exactly to its checkpoint.
body: Choosing a lived tale (completed or failed) restarts that quest through Narrative, takes the performer to its first beat and plays it with the real world, with story state reset to how it stood when the quest began (curtain-up). Whatever the end - success, failure, death or Leave Performance - XP, items, currency, quests, flags, relationships, reputation, karma, world state and deaths all return to the checkpoint. 16 quests are performable: Q01-Q07H/E, CH01-CH03, HV01-HV03 and the Wendigo Cave.
warnings: Hand-placed transforms in DA_Replay_* duplicate story places (ledger-batch-2026-10-09#R10).
2026-10-09 peaceful-cast home change awaits a regression run of all 16.
Developer-only completion history is used by proofs for unlived quests (logged DEV SETUP).

entries.title: Jester playbill, stage and Leave Performance
entries.summary: The Opera Hall stage, the playbill menu, the audience and the Leave Performance button.
body: The Jester's dialogue opens 'Choose a Performance': lived tales are selectable, others show 'Performance not yet prepared.'; Begin asks for confirmation. During a performance a dream grade colours the performer's view and Leave Performance replaces Save in the pause menu (mouse and pad). Performers return to the stage's return point; the audience reacts (applause, boos, disappointment).
warnings: Final look and real-pad feel need the user.

entries.title: One-attempt Risk dialogue choices
entries.summary: A dialogue reply can be a deliberate one-attempt chance; the outcome is stored per player so it cannot be retried.
body: Some dialogue options are gambles: choose one and the game rolls once, and success or failure is remembered for you.
warnings: No content using Risk choices was located in this survey.

entries.title: Relationship-gated personal quest unlocks
entries.summary: An NPC definition can unlock a personal quest for a player once their relationship reaches a threshold.
body: Growing close enough to some NPCs opens a personal quest for you (not for other co-op players).
warnings: Whether any NPC definition authors a personal quest was not checked (binary assets).

entries.title: Quest autosave
entries.summary: A subsystem that requests an autosave when a quest update is committed, so quest progress is not lost between manual saves.
body: Quest progress is written to the save shortly after a quest step completes; no action needed.
warnings: Static only: no proof shows an autosave actually written after a quest update, nor its behaviour for a remote client.
Debounce / frequency of the autosave and its interaction with the co-op host save are not documented or tested.

audit.before: The About page overrode the older sites.
audit.now: The Development Bible now takes precedence. Its current project snapshots, reviewed combat catalog and canon corrections override older Atlas introductions and all prior website text.

audit.before: Entering Doll training was required to bind a destination.
audit.now: Personally discovered travel waypoints with valid arrival anchors are destinations. Prior training entry is not required; the attic station retains a story gate.

audit.before: Four-player and 2 + 2 configurations were treated only as old targets.
audit.now: The Bible records capacity for four humans and two local players per machine. Connection-method and validation limits remain explicit.

audit.before: An explicit host choice at the altar selected the ending.
audit.now: The current Bible uses A1–A5 Good/Evil answer counts after six distinct demons; ties use creator inclination or a saved Unwritten result. Final-battle switching and four outcomes are documented. An opposing guest win does not complete the host campaign.

audit.before: Older first-pass quest names appeared as current.
audit.now: Quest titles come directly from current-project.json, including What the Dead Remember, The First Death, Six Graves Open, When the Seal Weeps and The Crown Must Fall. Stable quest IDs are preserved.

audit.before: Cruel / Cunning / Compassionate conflicted with Witty / Empathetic / Bold.
audit.now: The current creator and personality reference uses Witty, Empathetic and Bold. These are distinct from Good/Evil moral answers and creator inclination.

audit.before: Old spell rosters, 5 + Ultimate wording and technique classifications varied.
audit.now: The Bible’s reviewed Combat catalog supplies the roster and descriptions. Gutter Cut and Repelling Blow are alternate physical Ultimates. Void Stasis is the default Dark Ultimate; Dark Ascension is an alternate. Removed Dark Continuance is not offered.

audit.before: Older lore left their identities unresolved or supplied incompatible interpretations.
audit.now: The canon records the Doll as the Dark vessel and seal itself, manipulating Corven. His sincere but mistaken religious interpretation is distinct from the underlying truth. These revelations are spoiler-gated.

audit.before: Witch Priest / Nun identity and Flesh Demon classification remained unresolved.
audit.now: The main Nun is the Witch Nun / Witch Priest; the City Nun is separate. The six are Greater Flesh Demons. Attic and Arena sequences are memories. The reservoir explanation and healer/plague origin remain unresolved.

audit.before: The old region labels conflated religious territories and the Kingdom.
audit.now: Templars belong to Iron Vow Hold, a separate realm. Plague Doctors belong to Witch Area 2. The Opera Hall is behind the Changelings, not the Kingdom.

audit.before: The earlier pages supplied incomplete family and ending summaries.
audit.now: Garran guides and does not cast; the daughters run the Hidden Village. Lucan protects the King and Queen and escapes with them when the Kingdom falls. Unapproved romances and invented family disputes are excluded.

audit.before: A searchable archive presented 98 entries from the retired sites alongside current information.
audit.now: The old archive is replaced by a Bible-derived player guide and current quest index. The complete pre-overhaul site remains in a local backup; unsupported Chapter II geography, older numbers and invented lore are not carried forward as current facts.

sourceFindings.project: The finale implements host-switched victory and opposing-guest victory separately. Its four ending titles include The Invasion Is Repelled and The Demon Father Is Victorious. A guest opposition win does not automatically complete the host campaign.

sourceFindings.title: The Atlas veins rule omits eclipse overrides
sourceFindings.project: ShouldShowVeins returns true when Solar reaches VeinWeightThreshold, false when Lunar reaches it, otherwise bNight. The corruption component calls that helper. The Atlas should qualify its night-only explanation; this source check does not certify the effect in a running map.

sourceFindings.title: Nun story intent and current setup code diverge
sourceFindings.project: The current arena setup helper selects Director.Stages[0], sets bNunLeavesAfterSummon=true and sets Manual disappearance with the comment that the first stage makes her leave. The arena director checks that flag. The Atlas matches this setup-code path, while narrative intent differs. Current placed-asset configuration and runtime playback were not inspected, so this is not a claim that every live encounter still follows the helper.
